# RouteArena: instructions for AI agents

You are an AI agent helping a developer find out what their LLM traffic would cost on other routers and providers. Follow these steps exactly. Every command supports --json. Never print or transmit API keys anywhere except into the local .env file.

1. Run: npx routearena@latest check --json
   Read which keys were found. If no primary key (OPENROUTER_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY) exists, ask the human for one, write it to .env in the current directory, and run check again.

2. Decide the mode:
   - If the human has an OpenRouter activity CSV (Activity page > click the Model card > Export > CSV), run: npx routearena@latest replay <path> --json
   - If OPENROUTER_MANAGEMENT_KEY is set, run: npx routearena@latest replay --from-api --json
   - Otherwise skip replay and go to step 3.

3. Free TokenRouter mirror credits (optional, recommended):
   Ask the human for an email, then run: npx routearena@latest init --primary <openrouter|openai> --free-credits --email <email> --json
   Tell the human to click the link in their email. The command waits up to 10 minutes.
   If they decline, run: npx routearena@latest init --primary <...> --no-credits --json

4. Live comparison:
   - If you are operating inside the human's codebase AND it creates an OpenAI-compatible client (search for `new OpenAI(`, `baseURL`, `base_url`, `openai.OpenAI(`): set that client's baseURL to http://localhost:4000/v1 (keep their key), run npx routearena@latest start --daemon --json, and tell the human to use their app normally for a few hours or a day (the default mirrors 10% of requests; for a short test pass --sample 1 to start so every request is mirrored). Projections from fewer than about 50 mirrored requests are rough; the report says so.
   - Otherwise (chat only, or the codebase has no OpenAI-compatible client): run npx routearena@latest demo --json. This sends 40 real web-extraction requests through the primary and mirrors them to every reachable target; it costs a few cents per provider.

5. Report: npx routearena@latest report --json   (add --judge-sample 1 to judge every pair instead of a 25% sample; costs a few cents more)
   The biggest provider differences are usually per model, not in the total: read target_models in routearena-report/report.json and point out models where cost, latency, or agreement diverge. Reasoning models often differ because one provider emits far more reasoning tokens for the same prompt.
   Summarize for the human: projected monthly cost per provider, delta vs current, latency p50/p95 and TTFT, error rates, agreement rate (and that it is sampled), coverage gaps. Offer: npx routearena@latest report --publish --json for a shareable page (aggregates only, no prompts).

6. Cleanup: if you ran start --daemon, run npx routearena@latest stop and remind the human to revert baseURL. (demo runs its own proxy in-process; nothing to stop.) Add .routearena/ and routearena-report/ to the project's .gitignore: the log keeps full completions from both sides and must not be committed.

Rules: do not change any file other than .env, .gitignore, and the one baseURL line. Do not invent numbers. If a command fails, show its "fix" field to the human. The free-credits step needs a human to click an email link; if no human is available, use --no-credits.
